title: Kitchener indoor recreation complex and Rockway Centre plans
subtitle: Also covered: Oktoberfest and church noise exemptions, Festival of Neighbourhoods funding, and updated plumbing and drainage by-law.
overview: The committee recommended an operating model for the Kitchener Indoor Recreation Complex, due to open in 2026 {{vote:m5}}. Staff said the roughly $8.2 million annual cost would be covered by user fees and expected assessment growth, with no direct impact on existing taxpayers. The facility would be open 7 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week.

The committee also recommended that staff proceed with Phase 3 of the Rockway Centre redevelopment {{vote:m6}}. The request for proposals will set out requirements for a larger older adult centre and now includes a commercial kitchen, added by amendment. Proposals may include sites within 1.5 kilometres of the current centre.

Consent items were also recommended: noise exemptions for K-W Oktoberfest events and a church BBQ, redirecting $40,000 of annual capital funding from Festival of Neighbourhoods to the LoveMyHood Grant, and a repealed and replaced plumbing and drainage by-law. Council will consider these recommendations later.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the service-focused staffing and financial operating model for the Kitchener Indoor Recreation Complex and building its operating impacts into the 2026 and 2027 budgets.

The committee recommended proceeding with Phase 3, including RFP deliverables for a new older adult facility with a commercial kitchen, and allowing proposals for sites within 1.5 kilometres of the current centre.
The committee recommended redirecting the annual $40,000 capital allocation for Festival of Neighbourhoods to the LoveMyHood Grant for resident-led neighbourhood initiatives.
The committee recommended repealing Chapter 660 of the Municipal Code and replacing it with the updated plumbing and drainage by-law.
The committee recommended a Chapter 450 noise exemption for K-W Oktoberfest Inc. events at various clubs from September 26 to October 18, 2025.
The committee recommended a noise exemption for the Holy Trinity Serbian Orthodox Church's BBQ and Bull Roast on August 30 and 31, 2025, from 11 a.m. to 10 p.m.

debate: On the recreation complex, one councillor questioned midnight closing hours; staff cited a usage review showing early-morning walking and pool use and late-night adult league and cricket net use, and said demand may exceed the proposed hours.

Councillors asked how fees would work. Staff said youth groups would pay the lowest rate, bulk league bookings a middle rate, and out-of-town bookings the highest, so local residents are not crowded out.
Alcohol licensing at the complex would be available on an as-needed basis for major events rather than as standard concession sales; staff expected the revenue to be small.

On Rockway, staff said the current building has no gym and many small rooms, which limits programs and leaves waiting lists. They said an alternate site would keep the current centre open during construction and could be built faster.

The commercial kitchen amendment was supported as cheaper to build in now than to retrofit later, and for community rentals. Staff said a fully installed commercial kitchen could cost as much as $800,000, depending on the building.
